answer: Each identity must present a sequential state proof whose memory-hardness resists parallel evaluation and whose tenure is soulbound, so a farm cannot split one proof across a thousand machines and cannot hand the result to a fresh account. Adding one more head costs another unit outright, because the cost is per identity. The nebula is the sequential proof, the beacon the tenure it is bound to, and the anchor the memory-hardness that resists parallel evaluation; the nebula and the beacon are per identity, and it is the anchor that stops one proof serving a hundred clones.
